## Vocabulary

- **self**: Conditional nonlinear information transfer (13/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Conditional transfer entropy measures the information supplied by a source history about the target present after conditioning on the target history and specified additional process histories. Fully conditioned TE includes all other measured process histories in that conditioning set. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03229v4 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6793849/
- [statement] Interpret TE as a measured directed statistical dependency. A predictive dependency alone does not establish a physical causal mechanism: the estimator study explicitly avoids equating Wiener-style dependency with causal effect, and the high-order TE study distinguishes measured behavior from mechanism. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7597255/ · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03229v4

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] James, Barnett and Crutchfield argue that transfer entropy and causation entropy can overestimate information flow or underestimate influence. This is an attributed conceptual limitation, so a predictive dependency should not be presented unconditionally as a physical information-flow magnitude. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06479 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Kořenek, Sanda and Hlinka propose optimally conditioned TE to distinguish a genuinely synergistic causal set from separate individual causes: for exclusive disjunction, their abstract assigns the role to the multivariate set rather than the individual inputs. This is an attributed proposal, not a universal interpretation of standard conditional TE. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.08295 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer
- [statement] Baboukani and colleagues propose reducing dimensionality through non-uniform embedding before estimating directed dependencies. This is a proposed estimator design, rather than evidence that arbitrary history embeddings identify the same quantity. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13655 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer
- [statement] Transfer entropy has a model-free information-theoretic formulation that can assess linear and nonlinear interactions; nonlinear sensitivity depends on using an estimator appropriate to the dependence rather than imposing a linear-Gaussian model. JIDT documents KSG, kernel and linear-Gaussian estimator families. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7597255/ · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlizier/jidt/master/README.md, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/
- [statement] Additional conditioning does not necessarily reduce TE: redundant information can be removed, whereas synergistic information can become accessible. Conditional TE therefore includes source-unique information and source-conditioner synergy, rather than isolating only a pure two-variable contribution. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03229v4 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6793849/
- [statement] Stramaglia and colleagues propose searching conditioning subsets that minimize and maximize TE, rather than relying only on pairwise or fully conditioned TE, to expose redundant and synergistic effects. Their decomposition is a specific analysis proposal and should be identified as such. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03229v4 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Conditioning does not necessarily reduce measured dependence: conditional information can increase or decrease. Therefore a fully conditioned value and a pairwise value answer different predictive questions. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03229v4 · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer
- [statement] Bivariate TE can reflect indirect influences or shared drivers. Conditioning on relevant observed processes can separate those effects from the source-target dependency; the interpretation is relative to the variables and histories actually included. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7597255/, https://arxiv.org/abs/nlin/0001042
- [statement] Keskin and Aste use Schreiber’s general non-parametric formulation to quantify nonlinear transfer entropy, contrasting it with the autoregressive formulation used for linear transfer entropy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer
- [statement] The JIDT repository records adding conditional-transfer-entropy calculators implemented through underlying conditional-mutual-information calculators. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlizier/jidt/master/README.md · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer
- [statement] JIDT provides transfer entropy, mutual information and their conditional variants for discrete and continuous data, with Java implementations usable from languages including Python and R. This README establishes toolkit scope; it does not establish any particular installed version or estimator configuration. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlizier/jidt/master/README.md · keywords: Conditional nonlinear information transfer
